clue.text: What player won't want to receive? Guys maybe fail to answer

definitions.text: What player won't want to receive?

parts.note: Guy's is a famous London hospital, so Guys is an example of one
in a quiz you say pass when you cannot answer

explanation.surface: A riddle about an unwelcome delivery on the field, followed by a remark about blokes not replying.
explanation.walkthrough: Guy's Hospital is a teaching hospital in London; the missing apostrophe hides it among ordinary men.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby and football a hospital pass is a ball delivered just as the receiver is about to be tackled hard.

clue.text: Cartoon character: poet's devil child

parts.note: Homer, the Greek epic poet, with the possessive S
an imp is a small devil
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A cartoon figure described as the mischievous offspring of a poet.
explanation.definitionFit: The bumbling father in The Simpsons is one of television's best-known animated figures.

clue.text: Seafood one's taken from ships crossing border

indicators.note: the shortened ships go across the border, so they sit either side of it
the letter for one is removed from the word ships

parts.note: taken as written, before one letter is removed
one is the Roman numeral I
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: Seafood brought in by boats that cross a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Small edible crustaceans are a staple shellfish, a common kind of food from the sea.

clue.text: Old Peruvian showing where the baked beans are?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: belonging to the empire that ruled Peru before the Spanish
second meaning, read as two words: inside a tin

explanation.surface: A whimsical question about where an ancient Peruvian keeps the tinned beans.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second definition as a pun: split the answer into two words, meaning inside a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Inca empire ruled Peru before the Spanish conquest, so an ancient inhabitant there is Incan.

clue.text: A female keeping gents perhaps distant

indicators.note: the letters for a female hold the toilet inside them, together with A

parts.note: taken as written
the gents is a men's toilet, an example of a loo

explanation.surface: A woman holding some men at arm's length.
explanation.walkthrough: The gents is British slang for a men's public toilet; loo is the everyday British word for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reserved and standoffish is emotionally remote, the same sense as distant.

clue.text: Lifting cap, one means to punch peace-lovers

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting raises the word cap so it reads bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
fists are what you punch with

explanation.surface: Someone raising a hat and threatening to hit people who only want peace.
explanation.definitionFit: People who oppose war and violence on principle are those who love and pursue peace.

clue.text: So nicely balanced, my lime crystal shattered

indicators.note: broken into pieces, so the letters of these words are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written: these thirteen letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: An admiring remark about a lime-green crystal ornament that has unfortunately just broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something so that both halves mirror each other is the adverbial sense of being evenly balanced.

clue.text: Part of garden ruthlessly lifted up and transformed

indicators.note: in a down clue the concealed letters read upwards
the letters sit inside the run of garden ruthlessly

parts.note: the run of letters straddles the two words, from the end of garden into ruthlessly

explanation.surface: A section of the garden dug up and remade without mercy.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn into something else is to change form, as when milk is said to have gone off or changed.

clue.text: Sound of cattle crossing river by cricket club: love the country!

indicators.note: the cow's noise goes across the river letter, enclosing it

parts.note: cows say moo
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: Cows lowing beside the river and the cricket ground, prompting a cry of rural affection.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invites reading 'the country' as countryside, but it is a nation.
explanation.definitionFit: This North African kingdom is a nation, which is what 'the country' indicates here.

clue.text: Change your mind regarding university originally chosen for Wales

indicators.note: the gathered letters are altered into a new order
taking each word at its origin, its first letter

parts.note: the first letters of these four words are gathered
its first letter joins the others

explanation.surface: Someone reconsidering which university to pick and opting for one in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change your mind' reads as a phrase meaning reconsider; in fact 'Change' works alone on five initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Cymru is the Welsh-language name for the nation of Wales.

clue.text: From memory, an Italian native

parts.note: ROM is read-only memory in computing
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Italian recalled from memory.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone born in Rome, Italy's capital, is a native of that city.

clue.text: Rugby team, very loud, surrounding one youngster

indicators.note: the double forte letters go round the numeral for one

parts.note: FF is fortissimo in music
a teen is a young person

explanation.surface: A noisy rugby side crowding round a single youth.
explanation.definitionFit: A rugby union side fields this number of players, so the number names the team.

clue.text: Give out one's petition

parts.note: one is I, and the 's adds S
to sue is to petition or appeal formally

explanation.surface: Handing out a personal petition.
explanation.definitionFit: To distribute or release something officially, as with stamps or a statement, is to dispense it.

clue.text: Distraught re nurse, I can guarantee

definitions.note: the definition speaks as the answer, someone able to make sure

indicators.note: upset and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written: these seven letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: A patient reassuring an upset nurse about some matter.
explanation.definitionFit: One who makes certain of something is a guarantor, someone who can say they make things certain.

clue.text: Had yearning of French father and daughter

parts.note: de is French for of
sire means to father, or a male parent

explanation.surface: A French father and his daughter longing for something.
explanation.definitionFit: To have wanted or longed for something is the past tense of wishing for it.

clue.text: Playing card, most valuable one?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a card of the red suit marked with lozenges
second meaning: a precious gemstone, a most valuable stone

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'most valuable one' is loose: a gem, not the best card.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a card suit and the precious stone prized for its hardness and brilliance.

clue.text: Asian rips off French people

indicators.note: gone wrong or bad, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written: these nine letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone from Asia cheating some people from France.
explanation.definitionFit: Residents of the French capital are a group of people from France.

clue.text: Rodent performing in shop

parts.note: a rat is a rodent
a performer on stage is on

explanation.surface: A rat putting on a show inside a store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shop' is British slang meaning to inform on someone to the police, not a store.
explanation.definitionFit: To betray or inform against someone is the slang verb sense of grassing them up.

clue.text: Firm, small lettuce

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A crisp little lettuce.
explanation.definitionFit: Cos is a variety of crisp long-leaved salad plant, also called romaine.

clue.text: One on flight to look hard when speaking

indicators.note: the word is to be heard rather than read, giving a same-sounding word

parts.note: to stare is to look fixedly

explanation.surface: An air traveller staring intently while talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests air travel; here it is a flight of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A single step is one unit in a staircase, which is called a flight.

clue.text: One got our mail redirected to a remote region

indicators.note: sent on in a new direction, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written: these thirteen letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone receiving forwarded post that ended up far away.
explanation.walkthrough: The name is used in Britain as a byword for anywhere impossibly distant.
explanation.definitionFit: This Chinese territory beyond Mongolia is proverbially the most far-flung place imaginable.

clue.text: Stick something in one's mouth

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to glue or fasten
second meaning: the flesh around teeth

explanation.walkthrough: One short word serves as a verb for adhesion and a noun for what lines your jaw.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adhesive and the tissue holding teeth, as well as a sweet you chew.

clue.text: Scandinavian girl maybe riding out

indicators.note: put out of place, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written: these six letters are the fodder

explanation.surface: A Nordic girl perhaps out on horseback.
explanation.definitionFit: This given name is common in Sweden and Norway, so it is an example of a Nordic female name.

clue.text: Caught in dismay orotund dignitary

indicators.note: the letters are held within the words that follow

parts.note: the run of letters starts at the end of dismay and carries into orotund

explanation.surface: A pompous official trapped in a moment of dismay.
explanation.definitionFit: The civic head of a town council is a ceremonial official of local importance.
